_readme: Version pins for everything the onboard skill installs. READ THIS BEFORE CHOOSING ANY VERSION. Never infer a version from the client's existing dependencies, from a registry's 'latest', or from memory: both known onboarding defects came from guessing. CI asserts these values match the packages in this repo.

notes: No CommonJS build. The client's package.json needs "type": "module"; --require fails with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED.
Do NOT also install @opentelemetry/api. It is already a dependency, and a second copy at a different major silently breaks context propagation.
Version 0.1.2 or later is required: earlier versions do not register the ESM loader hook, so express/fastify/pg load unpatched and every server span is named after the bare method.

Adding this module raises go.opentelemetry.io/otel to v1.44.0 across the client's ENTIRE module graph, because Go selects the maximum required version. Expect an unrequested go.mod diff and say so in the PR body.
Go 1.25 is a hard floor set by OTel v1.44. A 1.22/1.24 toolchain fails to build.
go mod tidy is mandatory: Go refuses to build without the go.sum checksums, so a go.mod edit alone yields a patch that cannot compile.

goRouters._readme: Router middleware helpers. Prefer these over wiring the upstream otel* middleware by hand: correct span naming is baked in, and getting it wrong fills Mimir and gets writes rejected for every tenant on the platform.
notes: opentelemetry-go-contrib is pinned to the v0.69.0 line because that is the release series built against otel v1.44.0, which is what observability-go requires. Do not bump one without the other.
For a framework with no httpx package, find its contrib middleware and verify the span name reads 'GET /orders/{id}'. Never bare otelhttp.NewHandler on a server.
Do NOT install @digiform-by-gs/observability in a Next.js app. Its dependency tree (sdk-node, pino, auto-instrumentations) is exactly what Next's bundler and Edge runtime reject.

The 2.x line is required. @vercel/otel 1.x peers against OpenTelemetry SDK 1.x, which conflicts with the 2.x SDK this platform's stack is built on - and 'latest' resolution has already picked the wrong one once.
Custom spans work only in the Node runtime (export const runtime = 'nodejs'). Middleware runs on Edge and is effectively un-instrumentable.
Server logs are NOT correlated. Say so explicitly rather than implying full coverage.

lockfiles._readme: A dependency change without its lockfile is a broken patch, not an incomplete one. Both are non-negotiable.
lockfiles.node: After editing package.json run: npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts. Include package-lock.json in the patch. Verify with npm ci --dry-run - many production Dockerfiles run npm ci, which fails outright when the two files disagree.
lockfiles.go: After editing go.mod run: go mod tidy. Include go.sum in the patch. Verify with go build ./...
